messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — Sev2: elevated 5xx + timeouts observed from edge -> gateway. Alert fired at 2024-09-14T12:19:15Z. Affected path: /api/generate (host: api.redwood.example). 5xx rate jumped ~0.2% -> 7% in ~4m. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/example/alerts/1729005555. Paging oncall: @Alex K and @Mira S. Please ack and triage.

Alex K: acked — I’m oncall. Pulling logs + envoy admin stats now. ping @Sam T for LB infra access.

Mira S: ack — will start tracing a sample request. Any users reporting errors? support says ~10 accounts reported timeouts in last 10m.

Alex K: looking at edge -> envoy stats:
```
# query envoy admin
curl -s http://envoy-admin.internal:9901/stats?filter=cluster\.|listener\.|route\.
# key observed: cluster.api_upstream.upstream_rq_5xx: 1270
# cluster.api_upstream.upstream_rq_5xx_ratio: 0.068
```
There’s a recent config push 10m ago: xds version v2024-09-14-12:08 from infra-deploy pipeline.

Sam T: I can confirm a route weight change was rolled out in that push — we flipped traffic to a new subset (canary) and enabled retries on the route. pinging infra deployment logs.

Lee R: noticed retry loop amplification in logs. Example from gateway logs:
```
[2024-09-14T12:18:47Z] upstream request id=abc123 status=502 attempt=2 total_attempts=5 latency_ms=1200
[2024-09-14T12:18:48Z] upstream request id=abc124 status=502 attempt=3 total_attempts=5 latency_ms=1300
```
Requests are being retried aggressively which is amplifying load and hitting circuit breakers -> more 5xx.

Mira S: can we see the envoy route config snippet? I want to confirm retry config + per_try_timeout.

Alex K: pasted relevant route fragment from xDS snapshot:
```
route: {
  match: { prefix: "/api/" }
  route: {
    cluster: "api_upstream"
    retry_policy: {
      retry_on: "5xx,connect-failure,reset"
      num_retries: 5
      per_try_timeout: 2s
    }
    request_mirror_policies: [ ... ]
  }
}

circuit_breakers: {
  default: { max_connections: 200, max_pending_requests: 20, max_retries: 2 }
}
```
Num_retries=5 and per_try_timeout 2s + circuit breaker limits are low — this combination explains the cascade.

Sam T: recommendation: temporarily disable retries on that route and increase circuit breaker pending_requests to reduce immediate pressure. I can apply a quick xds patch to set `num_retries: 0` and bump `max_pending_requests: 200` for cluster api_upstream. Will do a canary push to 1 node then global if green.

Alex K: before you push, we should also reduce canary route weight back to 0 and route traffic evenly to healthy pool. If retry disabled + weight rollback, we expect immediate drop in amplified load.

Jordan P: tagging infra oncall @Lee R because we might need to roll back the deployment that changed the backend subset if traffic still degrades.

Sam T: executing patch now (will use infra canary). Command:
```
# apply xds patch (dry-run then apply)
curl -X PATCH https://xds-api.internal/configs/route/api -d '{"retry_policy":{"num_retries":0}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
Applying to canary node id env-canary-3...

incident-bot: ACTION — xds patch started: xds/task/8791 (Sam T)

Alex K: watching metrics. Also running quick `curl` to admin to ensure stats move:
```
watch -n 5 "curl -s 'http://envoy-admin.internal:9901/stats?filter=cluster.api_upstream.upstream_rq_5xx'"
```

~+4m after patch

Mira S: early signal looks good — 5xx back down to ~1.1% and latency dropping. Support notes fewer new complaints.

Sam T: canary apply succeeded, rolling patch to remaining nodes. Lowering route weight for the new subset to 0 now.

Lee R: I increased max_pending_requests to 200 on cluster api_upstream. Circuit breakers are less trippy now.

Alex K: checking logs — retry attempts gone, majority of upstream 5xx resolved. We still have a handful of timeouts from a small backend shard.

Jordan P: opening a post-incident task: infra rollback + root cause analysis of why canary had unhealthy capacity and why retries were enabled by default. Assigning to Sam T and Lee R. Ticket: https://tickets.redwood/INC-1729005555

Mira S: draft customer-impact blurb for status page:
- Incident start: 2024-09-14T12:19:15Z
- Mitigation applied: 2024-09-14T12:25:40Z (retry disabled + circuit breaker relax + canary weight rollback)
- Impact: transient elevated 5xx/timeouts for API users (~0.2% -> 7% peak). ~10 customer-reported failures.
- Status: mitigated, backend shard under investigation.

Alex K: Handing off to infra for follow-up. Oncall clear for now but I’ll stay as responder until RCA.

Sam T: noted. Will keep a watch for 30m then create RCA doc. Initial hypothesis: canary capacity mis-sizing + aggressive retries in route config amplified failures into a cascade. Follow-ups: revert default retry policy in deployment pipeline, add QA for canary capacity, add dashboard alert for sudden retry count spike.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded to Sev3 (mitigated) at 2024-09-14T12:28:50Z. If new 5xx > 1% sustained for 5m, reopen.

Alex K: final summary for handoff ->
- Root cause (working): new canary subset with insufficient capacity + route config enabling retries by default.
- Mitigation: disabled retries, bumped pending requests CB, rolled canary weight back to 0.
- Customer impact: brief window of increased 5xx/timeouts, now resolved.
- Next actions: infra to RCA + fix pipeline, product/support to notify affected customers if needed.

Mira S: adding logs + admin dumps to the incident ticket.

Jordan P: thanks everyone. If support needs a polished customer message I can help edit. :thumbsup:

Alex K: closing thread for oncall handoff — leaving incident ticket open for RCA. If anything regresses, re-page.
